paper_metadata.title: Modification of a Quantum-inspired Genetic Algorithm for Numerical Optimization Using Qudit under Conditions of Simulating Quantum Decoherence

summary: The paper proposes MQIGA, a classical quantum-inspired optimization algorithm using qudit-based state simulation and simulated decoherence, and evaluates it on 8 benchmark functions, 3 hybrid flow-shop scheduling instances, and 3 regression datasets. On the benchmark suite, MQIGA reaches near-zero best values for f1–f7 at n=2 and n=15, with runtimes around 1.03–1.29 s on the benchmark tests; for ELM tuning it achieves the best MAE on CPU Performance (5.3), Auto Imports (2080), and Boston Housing (1.86).

experiments.description: Modified quantum-inspired genetic algorithm (MQIGA) for numerical optimization using qudits under simulated quantum decoherence, evaluated on benchmark optimization functions, a hybrid flow-shop scheduling cost objective, and ELM hyperparameter tuning.

algorithm.variant: Modified Quantum-Inspired Genetic Algorithm (MQIGA) with qudit-based state representation and simulated decoherence
algorithm.parameter_initialization: qudit states initialized via Hadamard-like superposition and random rotation angles theta drawn from tau*N(0,1)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: classical binary chromosomes derived from qudit state probabilities; qudit length 5 used to generate classical binary genes
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize f(x) for benchmark test functions; maximize cost-based hybrid flow-shop objective CL + CE + CR + CP; minimize MAE for ELM tuning (reported as improved forecasting accuracy)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: for optimization functions, values outside search range are replaced with random values from X; crossover/mutation guided by best chromosome; no explicit penalty formulation reported

problem_instance.description: Benchmark optimization on 8 test functions (2D and 15D), hybrid flow-shop scheduling cost optimization, and regression forecasting with compact ELM on three public datasets
problem_instance.dataset_name: Rastrigin, Sphere, Griewank, Schwefel 1.2, Ackley, Rosenbrock, Zakharov, Styblinski-Tang, CPU Performance, Auto Imports, Boston Housing, J10c5a2, J10c5b1, J10c5c1

dataset_specification.benchmark_name: standard optimization benchmarks; UCI-style regression datasets; flow-shop control tasks
dataset_specification.preprocessing: for ELM, 10-fold cross-validation; for optimization, 50 repeated runs; for scheduling, 10 repeated runs

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: benchmark functions evaluated at specified dimensionalities; ELM uses 10-fold cross-validation; scheduling uses control-task parameter scenarios
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 50 independent runs for benchmark functions; Wilcoxon signed-rank test; convergence curves; 10-fold cross-validation for ELM; 10 runs for scheduling tasks

noise_model.noise_type: simulated quantum decoherence; normal random noise N(0,1) applied to rotation angles

implementation_details.classical_solver: mealpy library classical optimizers (GA, DE, PSO, NRO) and ACOR baseline for scheduling; compact ELM baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: random initialization of qudit rotation angles; conversion of measured qudit probabilities to binary chromosomes; replacement of out-of-range values with random values from search domain
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: best-solution tracking; averaging over runs; Wilcoxon test; convergence plots; MAE computation for ELM

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: convergence curves reported; MQIGA generally faster and higher than baselines

speedup_claims.factor: faster than qiga and ga on benchmark functions; runtime advantage in 3/8 two-dimensional cases and 3/8 fifteen-dimensional cases
speedup_claims.conditions: benchmark optimization functions with pop_size=100, gen_max=450, 50 runs
speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic speedup proven; runtime advantage is instance-dependent and not universal.

speedup_claims.factor: faster than qiga and ga on all benchmark functions in reported comparisons
speedup_claims.conditions: benchmark functions f1-f8 at n=2 and n=15
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states MQIGA is faster than QIGA and GA for all benchmark functions, but not always faster than DE, PSO, or NRO.

speedup_claims.factor: better forecasting accuracy (lowest MAE) on all three datasets
speedup_claims.baseline_method: elm, qiga-elm, ga-elm, de-elm, pso-elm, nro-elm
speedup_claims.conditions: 10-fold cross-validation on CPU Performance, Auto Imports, Boston Housing
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an accuracy improvement, not a computational speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Classical CPU-only implementation in JupyterLab; no quantum hardware resources reported.
limiting_factors: No gate-based quantum hardware or circuit is used
The method is a classical quantum-inspired heuristic with qudit simulation
No asymptotic quantum speedup analysis is provided
Performance is empirical and mixed across baselines
Classical baselines remain competitive or better on several metrics

notes: No physical quantum hardware is used; the paper is a quantum-inspired classical algorithm paper, so hardware.type is not specified.
num_qubits is not explicitly reported because the method uses qudits and simulated quantum states rather than a gate-based qubit circuit.
circuit_depth is not a gate-circuit depth; the paper reports algorithmic generations/iterations and qudit rotation operations, so this field is left null.
speedup_order inferred as none_proven because the paper reports empirical improvements over classical baselines but no asymptotic quantum speedup analysis.
The paper claims empirical superiority of MQIGA over QIGA and some classical optimizers on selected tasks, but the evidence is mixed and does not establish practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Classical baseline algorithms compared against MQIGA on benchmark functions, production scheduling, and ELM tuning.

algorithm.variant: GA, DE, PSO, NRO, ACOR, and compact ELM baseline

hyperparameters.acor: continuous ant colony optimization baseline for scheduling

key_results: MQIGA outperforms QIGA, GA, DE, PSO, and NRO on many benchmark metrics, but not uniformly on all cases.
For n=15, GA is best on f8 mean value, and PSO/DE are best on some runtime cases.
For scheduling, MQIGA is best on J10c5a2 runtime, while ACOR is faster on all three tasks.
For ELM tuning, MQIGA-ELM has the lowest MAE on CPU Performance (5.3), Auto Imports (2080), and Boston Housing (1.86).
